notes: On 3 January 2023, around 400 protesters including staff and health workers gathered outside Howard Brown Health clinics in several locations across Chicago (Illinois) to protest the recent layoffs of 60+ employees during contract negotiations. The Illinois Nurses Association helped organize these demonstrations.

Around 7 January 2023 (weekend of), demonstrators including students and affiliates of Time Youth Dothan gathered at the Houston County Courthouse in Dothan (Alabama) to call for an end to gun violence. This follows the recent fatal shootings of some youth members of Time Youth Dothan.

On 17 January 2023, an unreported number of workers alongside members of the Union of Southern Service Workers demonstrated outside of Dollar General in Irmo (South Carolina) to call for an improvement of working conditions and pay at the company. The protest took place as part of a two-day strike organized by two workers at the store.

On 24 January 2023, hundreds of American Airlines flight attendants picketed at Dallas/Fort Worth International Airport (Texas) to protest for pay raises. This demonstration was part of a nation-wide demonstration organized by the Association of Flight Attendants at around a dozen airports.

On 20 May 2023, 10 demonstrators, including Proud Boys and members of Christian groups, gathered at the Unitarian Universalist Community Church of Southwest Michigan in Portage (Michigan) to demonstrate against a drag event being held at the church. Some were dressed in Bud Light costumes to rally against Bud Light's partnership with a trans social media influencer. They were met by 40-50 counter-demonstrators who rallied in support of the event and in solidarity with the LGBTQ+ community. Antifascists, anarchists, socialists, Satanists, and members of the Unitarian Universalist Church were among those present. A fight erupted and one anti-LGBTQ+ demonstrator was arrested for assaulting somebody. There were no reported injuries.

source: New York Times; State (Columbia); WLTX News 19
notes: On 29 May 2023, demonstrators gathered outside of a Shell gas station in Columbia (South Carolina) to memorialize and call for justice in the case of a 14-year-old Black teenager that was fatally shot by the owner of the Shell gas station due to the owner suspecting that the teen had stolen water bottles. Authorities believe that the teenager was innocent. Some demonstrators vandalized the store, shattered windows, and stole merchandise. Earlier in the day, a peaceful demonstration took place (coded separately).

On 29 May 2023, demonstrators marched from the US Capitol to the DC Jail in Washington DC - Southeast (District of Columbia) in support of people who were detained inside due to their participation in the 6 January 2021 Capitol Riot. They also memorialized deceased insurrectionist Ashli Babbit, whose mother was also present. Nearby, several counter-demonstrators rallied against those detained and in support of the prosecution of 6 January 2021 insurrectionists. A counter-demonstrator who had been yelling at the demonstrators through a megaphone was confronted by Ashli Babbit's mother, who proceeded to slam the megaphone into the ground before striking her and shoving the counter-demonstrator several times. Babbitt's mother was arrested on 30 May and later released. Charges against her were later dropped.

On 10 June 2023, a man who had come to show opposition to the Hot Springs pride parade in Hot Springs (Arkansas) was arrested after assaulting a man who was attending the parade. The parade attendee was punched in the face and suffered minor injuries to his eye, as well as chipped teeth. Witnesses claimed the assault took place because the attendee tried to stop children participating in the parade from seeing a 'very provocative' sign being held by the man who carried out the assault.

On 12 June 2023, a perpetrator approached a 21-year-old man, made anti-LGBTQ+ remarks and punched him in the head multiple times on First Avenue in New York - Manhattan (New York) in an unprovoked attack. The victim suffered a nasal bone fracture and other facial injuries. NYPD are investigating the incident as a hate crime.

On 25 September 2023, a group of men gathered outside the Univerity of Kentucky in Lexington (Kentucky) to demonstrate against women in general, holding signs that said, 'Women are property,' 'Are you rape bait?' and 'God hates all workers of iniquity, Psalm 5:5.' A video appeared to show a passing student struggle with one of the men holding a sign, at which point the man appears to punch the student in the head.

On 11 January 2024, protesters rallied in Northampton (Massachusetts) to demand the closure of Guantanamo Bay detention camp due to poor living conditions, as well as what they claimed is 'torture methods and abuse.' No More Guantanamos, Witness Against Torture, CodePink, and Amherst Amnesty International Group 128 organized the rally.

Around 18 January 2024 (as reported), White Lives Matter affiliates gathered in Alabama (coded as Montgomery (Alabama)) to demonstrate in favor of White Lives Matter, hold antisemitic signs, and promote the group.

source: 5 On Your Side; KMOV4; KWMU; St. Louis Post-Dispatch
notes: On 18 January 2024, hundreds of students walked out of class to hold a rally at Francis Howell High School and Francis Howell North High School in Saint Charles (Missouri) to protest against the Francis Howell School Board's decision to remove Black History and Black Literature courses due to the courses' connection to the 'Social Justice Standards: The Teaching Tolerance Anti-Bias Framework.'
On 6 January 2022, dozens of protesters held a 'pro-democracy' demonstration in Oreland (Pennsylvania) as part of nationwide events commemorating the anniversary of the 6 January 2021 Capitol riots.

On 6 January 2022, demonstrators staged a 'Day of Remembrance and Action' rally and 'Defend our Democracy' vigil at Peace Corner in Memorial Park in downtown DeKalb (Illinois) in support of voting rights legislation. The DeKalb County League of Women Voters and REACT (Responsive Engagement Activating Civic Talent) organized the event to commemorate the 1-year anniversary of the Capitol riots.

On 16 January 2022, dozens of people gathered outside the Islamic Cultural Center in New York - Bronx (New York) to urge New York City leaders to investigate the owners of the Twin Parks North West apartment and to mourn the 15 people who died in the Twin Parks fire.

On 23 March 2022, a Warrior Met Coal natural gas pipeline that ran along Hannah Creek Road in Brookwood (Alabama) was damaged by an explosive device in what police say was an act of vandalism by yet unknown perpetrator(s). An investigation is ongoing. This comes amidst a labor dispute between Warrior Met Coal and the United Mine Workers of America that has lasted since April 2021, and both have issued statements condemning the property destruction.

On 1 April 2022, a group of six people attacked a Hasidic Jewish man in front of an apartment building at 58 Gerry St. in Williamsburg in New York - Brooklyn (New York) in what appears to be an antisemitic hate crime. The man suffered minor injuries to his mouth and was treated at the scene. One of the perpetrators was later arrested and charged with gang assault and assault as a hate crime.

source: HuffPost; Clarion Ledger; Network Contagion Research Institute; WHDH Channel 7
notes: On 24 June 2022, people gathered outside of the Jackson Women's Health Organization in Jackson (Mississippi) to promote 'pro-life' policies and an end to abortion. Several individuals were 'harassing' those entering the clinic. Police arrived to monitor the situation when clinic workers reported that one of the anti-abortion demonstrators backed his vehicle up and hit one of the clinic's volunteers.

On 30 July 2022, a group of teenagers yelled homophobic slurs and assaulted a LGBT+ couple in Sandy (Utah). One of the victims suffered a concussion and some brain swelling after being punched. The alleged perpetrator was taken into custody by the police. No fatalities were recorded.

On 31 July 2022, a woman repeatedly struck a volunteer with Students for Life Action on the head in Leawood (Kansas). The volunteer was going door-to-door advocating for 'pro-life' policies ahead of a constitutional amendment vote. The woman was arrested for misdemeanor battery. The volunteer had no injuries.

On 7 August 2022, 7 teenagers followed two gay men, then proceeded to punch them several times in Washington DC - Northwest (District of Columbia) while saying 'monkeypox f*****.' The men had to go to the hospital where one received stitches. The incident is being investigated as a potential hate crime.

On 3 January 2021, people gathered for a protest in Portland (Oregon) in favor of schools remaining closed during the coronavirus pandemic. The protest was separate from a protest in favor of opening schools on the same day.

On 3 January 2021, more than 100 people, led by five supporters, gathered in McAlester (Oklahoma) to conclude a four-day march that began in Oklahoma City to demand clemency for Julius Jones. Jones maintains his innocence after being found guilty by a jury of murder in 2002.
On 4 January 2021, a dozen teachers and parents rallied in Gilbert (Arizona) against schools reopening after the winter break due to high coronavirus cases.
On 4 January 2021, a small group with Down Home NC protested outside the courthouse in Burlington (North Carolina) against the proposed expansion of the Haywood County Detention Center.
On 5 January 2021, family and friends gathered for a 'Justice for Lace' event in Ishpeming (Michigan) to demand justice for Lacie Borchert, a 25-year-old woman who was killed on November 27th.

On 5 January 2021, less than a dozen people with Preserve Our Rural Communities and Protect San Benito rallied outside the county superior court in Hollister (California) against alleged reduction in environmental measures led by supervisors and developers.
On 6 January 2021, around 15 people rallied in Northampton (Massachusetts) calling for democracy to be upheld while certifying electoral college votes for President-Elect Joe Biden.

source: Crowd Counting Consortium; Northeast Mississippi Daily Journal
notes: On 6 January 2021, about 20 people, including members of a local animal rights group, gathered on the Court Square in Fulton (Mississippi) in protest of animal cruelty, following two recent incidents pet shootings by local officers.

source: Crowd Counting Consortium; Seattle Department of Transportation
notes: On 7 January 2021, black-clad demonstrators marched through the streets in Seattle (Washington) in support of Black Lives Matter movement, against racism and police violence, and demanding justice for Jacob Blake and Dolal Idd.

On 7 January 2021, members of 'Together We Will - Harford County/Upper Chesapeake' gathered outside the Bel Air district office of U.S. Rep. Andy Harris in Bel Air (Maryland) demanding Congressman Andy Harris resign for having voted to object to the certification of the Electoral College votes.

On 9 January 2021, a caravan of 40 cars, led by several local groups like the Madison chapters of Democratic Socialists of America and Allies for Black Lives, drove around Madison (Wisconsin) to call for the resignation of U.S. Sen. Ron Johnson after the riot at the U.S. Capitol on January 6th.

On 9 January 2021, dozens of people gathered outside Rep. Jeff Van Drew's office in Mays Landing (New Jersey) demanding his resignation in response to him supporting an objection to electoral college votes certifying election results for President-Elect Joe Biden.

On 9 January 2021, around 150 people rallied in Manchester (Connecticut) in support of a woman who was spit on by an anti-vaccination protester while at a Black Lives Matter rally at the State House in Hartford on 5 January 2021.
On 9 January 2021, dozens of people marched in Perrine (Florida) to call for an end to violence in South Florida following several deadly shootings at the start of the new year.

On 10 January 2021, more than 50 people took part in a Black Lives Matter protest in Post Office Square in Belfast (Maine) and also protested against the violence at the Capitol in Washington DC during the election certification for President-Elect Joe Biden on 6 January 2021.

source: AM New York; CBS2 (New York); Outlive Them NYC
notes: On 10 January 2021, over 200 people, including members of Outlive Them NYC and United Against Racism and Fascism NYC marched from Columbus Circle to Times Square to Madison Square Park in New York - Manhattan (New York) demanding President Trump be removed from office immediately in response to the violence at the Capitol in Washington DC on 6 January 2021. People chanted, 'Trump, Pence, out now', 'Our city, our streets!', and 'What's that noise, fuck the Proud boys.' A group of demonstrators attacked a woman who was filming the demonstration. Demonstrators reportedly became angry and threw a raw egg at her, hit her with an umbrella, skateboard, sprayed her with aerosol, and rubbed a dirty diaper in her face. There were no serious injuries. The march was supposed to be a counter-demonstration organized in response to a proposed Proud Boys/MAGA demonstration at Columbus Circle that never happened.

On 12 January 2021, members of the teacher's union in about 50 cars protested outside a Middle School in Newark (Delaware) to call for board members to switch to virtual learning during the coronavirus pandemic.
On 12 January 2021, around a dozen people protested in Columbia (South Carolina) to call for the statue of Ben Tillman to be removed due to his history of racism.

On 13 January 2021, several dozen people gathered outside the federal courthouse in Columbia (Missouri) to demand the resignation of Senator Josh Hawley after Hawley objected to President-elect Joe Biden's electoral college victory and in response to a mob breaching the Capitol in an attempt to overturn the electoral results.

On 16 January 2021, eight people gathered in Carthage Square in Carthage (Missouri) to demand the resignation of Senator Josh Hawley after Hawley objected to President-elect Joe Biden's electoral college victory and in response to a mob breaching the Capitol in an attempt to overturn the electoral results.

On 16 January 2021, about 20 people, including the local NAACP President, gathered outside of a supermarket in Houma (Louisiana) in protest of the store co-owner's participation in the Pro-Trump rally, which devolved into a riot in DC. The group called for the boycott of the store.

On 16 January 2021, about 100 students and supporters gathered in Coeur d'Alene (Idaho) for a rally to support LGBT youth. This rally followed a 'Stop the Child Abuse' rally held on 11 January, which was organized to demonstrate against a situation involving a school counsellor who spoke to a transgender student about wanting to transition.

source: Crowd Counting Consortium; Times of Northwest Indiana
notes: On 17 January 2021, 10-15 people including teachers participated in a caravan that passed by school board members' homes in Chicago (Illinois) with signs that read, 'SCEC respect us!', 'Grads not graves' and 'Remote learning saves lives' to show support for a safe return-to-school plan and to stand against returning too soon amid the coronavirus pandemic.
On 18 January 2021, about 100 people marched in Wilmington (Delaware) to call for peace and a reduction of gun violence, as well as in honor of Martin Luther King Jr.

On 18 January 2021, about 30 people gathered outside of a church in Knoxville (Tennessee) to show support for the Black Lives Matter movement and call for an end to racism after their Black Lives Matter banner was stolen.

On 18 January 2021, about 30 people staged a vigil and rally in Casa Grande (Arizona) in memory of Martin Luther King, Jr. and in support of the Black Lives Matter movement, peace, unity, and justice.

On 19 January 2021, more than two dozen people, organized by a local Democrat group, gathered at a church in Diamondhead (Mississippi) to honor the lives lost amid the coronavirus pandemic in solidarity with the memorial in Washington DC.

On 22 January 2021, a group of about 30 people marched in Lawton (Oklahoma) in support of the Black Lives Matter movement and against the death of Zonterius Johnson, a Black man who was shot and killed by a police officer earlier in the week.

On 23 January 2021, more than a dozen people, including BLM members, gathered outside of U.S. Representative Mo Brook's office in downtown Huntsville (Alabama) to call for his resignation after he allegedly incited the riot at the U.S. Capitol on 6 January.

On 25 January 2021, about 30 high school students protested in Columbia (South Carolina) against returning to school in-person during the coronavirus pandemic and to call for district leaders to bear safety in mind when making decisions about moving back to in-person learning.

On 13 March 2021, a group of about 100 people gathered for a demonstration in the evening organized by Black Unity and additionally held a vigil for Breonna Taylor at Revolution Hall in Portland - Southeast (Oregon) and then marched to the Burnside Bridge to release lanterns for Taylor. The group, who were dressed in black bloc, then marched to the justice center in Portland. The demonstration turned violent as demonstrators, including Antifa, broke windows at the justice center in the evening.

On 27 March 2021, Proud Boys held a small Easter egg hunt demonstration in Schaumburg (Illinois) against President Biden and against wearing masks during the coronavirus pandemic which was counter-demonstrated. An altercation occurred between a Proud Boy and a counter-demonstrator after an apparent skirmish over a flag. The Proud Boys member repeatedly punched the counter-demonstrator. The Proud Boys member involved was present at the 6 January incident at the US Capitol Building and is currently planning a run for government.

On 9 July 2021, a transgender individual was physically assaulted in Washington DC (District of Columbia) by a group of people after the group questioned the individual's gender identity and attacked them, requiring hospitalization. Police say they are investigating the incident as a hate crime.

On 31 July 2021, a few dozen people without masks gathered for a demonstration in Moscow (Idaho) against having to wear masks during the coronavirus pandemic. At one point, two men, one anti-mask demonstrator and another with a mask, started arguing and got into a physical fight. It is not clear what led to the altercation.

On 31 August 2021, more than 1000 students gathered outside the Phi Gamma Delta fraternity house in Iowa City (Iowa) to urge the university to remove the Phi Gamma Delta fraternity from campus after a petition alleged that two members of the fraternity sexually assaulted a student in September 2020. Some people broke windows, kicked down doors, and spray-painted on the house and another house. Additionally, some demonstrators also flipped cars in front of the houses.

On 29 October 2021, a Black man who was riding a bike was attacked by a white man in Seabrook (Texas). The perpetrator is claimed to have stopped his car to question the victim's presence in the neighborhood, used racial slurs, and then physically attacked the victim. The victim was cut multiple times requiring stitches and was also left with a broken tooth, fractured cheek bone, and burst blood vessel in the eye. The suspect was arrested and charged with misdemeanor aggravated assault.

On 19 April 2020, inmates attacked a prison guard at Sumter Correctional Institute in Bushnell (Florida) amid concerns that the prison was becoming a hotspot for the coronavirus pandemic. The guard was hospitalized with non-lethal injuries. No casualties.

On 20 April 2020, roughly 40 youth prisoners started a riot at the Bridge City Center in Bridge City (Louisiana) in response to fears about insufficient health protocols during the ongoing coronavirus pandemic. The riot was quelled by the Parish Sheriff's Office and its SWAT team after prison guards lost control of the situation. No fatalities reported.

On 30 May 2020, less than 20 demonstrators gathered in Gainesville (Georgia) in support of the Black Lives Matter movement and against police brutality and the death of George Floyd. They damaged six police cars. Ten people was arrested.

source: News Journal (Wilmington-DE); US Press Freedom Tracker; Committee to Protect Journalists
notes: On 30 May 2020, more than 1,000 people demonstrated in downtown Wilmington (Delaware) in support of the Black Lives Matter movement and against Police brutality and the death of George Floyd. The demonstration turned violent when rioters set fire to trash bins and smashed windows. Two journalists were allegedly attacked by the demonstrators. No injuries reported.

source: Times of Northwest Indiana; Crowd Counting Consortium
notes: On 31 May 2020, around 300 people demonstrated at Southlake Mall in Hobart (Indiana) in support of the Black Lives Matter movement and against police brutality and the death of George Floyd. The Lake County Tactical Unit team was deployed to aid police. Demonstrators threw a plastic water bottle filled with rocks at police, injuring an officer. Police deployed tear gas and rubber bullets and made 10 arrests.

On 31 May 2020, people staged a demonstration in Tukwila (Washington) in support of the Black Lives Matter movement and against Police brutality and the death of George Floyd, a black man killed by police in Minneapolis. The demonstration turned violent when people looted several stores and police responded by spraying tear gas, arresting several demonstrators.

On 31 May 2020, more than 100 people demonstrated in Vallejo (California) in support of the Black Lives Matter movement and against police brutality and the death of George Floyd. The demonstration turned violent when the group arrived outside the Vallejo police headquarters and began throwing rocks and bottles at police. A police vehicle was damaged after a rock was thrown into the windshield. Officers intervened and dispersed the crowd with tear gas, flashbangs, and less lethal force.

On 31 May 2020, thousands of people demonstrated in Portland (Oregon) in support of the Black Lives Matter movement and against police brutality and the death of George Floyd, a black man killed by police in Minneapolis. A group of demonstrators later in the day threw water bottles at police officers and set off fireworks and 'aerial mortars', prompting police to use flash bangs and tear gas to disperse the crowd and arrest 14.

On 1 June 2020, an unreported number of people stage a demonstration in Northampton (Massachusetts) in support of the Black Lives Matter movement and against police brutality and the death of George Floyd. Rioters threw water bottles and rock at police officers. Four police cars were damaged with smashed windshields and punctured tires. Police station windows were broken. No injuries or arrests reported.

On 1 June 2020, an unreported number of people staged a demonstration in Kalamazoo (Michigan) in support of the Black Lives Matter movement and against police brutality and the death of George Floyd. Rioters smashed windows, destroyed property and spraying-painting buildings. Police used tear gas to control the crowd. No arrests reported.

On 1 June 2020, over 100 people demonstrated in Columbia (Missouri) in support of the Black Lives Matter movement and against police brutality and the death of George Floyd, a black man killed by police. 2 cars ran into demonstrators at the same location with no report of serious injuries. After midnight, the door of a Walgreens was reportedly smashed by demonstrators.
tags: car ramming; Terrorist activity; crowd size=medium

notes: On 2 June 2020, about a hundred people demonstrated in Kalamazoo (Michigan) in support of the Black Lives Matter movement and against police brutality and the death of George Floyd. Rioters smashed windows and spray painted some buildings. Police used tear gas and mace pellets to disperse the crowd.

On 6 June 2020, 3000 people demonstrated in Oklahoma City (Oklahoma) in support of the Black Lives Matter movement, and against police brutality and the death of George Floyd. Sheriff deputies kneeled with the people. Later, rioters began throwing water bottles. Police intervened with tear gas.

On 6 June 2020, people rioted in Merrick (New York) as part of national unrest in support of the Black Lives Matter movement and against police brutality. Nearly a dozen people were arrested and two police officers were injured.
On 14 June 2020, several hundreds people staged a protest in Jackson (Wyoming) in support of the Black Lives Movement and against police brutality and the death of George Floyd.

On 14 June 2020, hundreds of people marched in protest in Minden (Louisiana) calling for peace and social justice in the city amidst the death of George Floyd by police and nationwide Black Lives Matter demonstrations.
On 19 June 2020, people staged a protest to mark Juneteenth in Montville (New Jersey).

On 19 June 2020, about a dozen people staged a demonstration in Cheyenne (Wyoming) to commemorate Juneteenth and in support of the Black Lives Matter movement and against police brutality and the death of George Floyd.

On 20 June 2020, hundreds of people participated in the rally 'Friends for Justice' in Bountiful (Utah), in support of the Black Lives Matter movement and against Police brutality and the death of George Floyd.

On 20 June 2020, hundred people staged a protest in Staunton (Illinois) to celebrate Juneteenth and in support of the Black Lives Matter movement and against police brutality and the death of George Floyd.

On 20 June 2020, a few hundred BLM protesters and the Columbiana County Unorganized Militia joined together for a protest in Lisbon (Ohio), calling for an end to racism and in support of a local FedEx driver who says he was called a racial slur and spat on in the community.
On 25 June 2020, people staged a protest in Manchester (Maryland) in support of the Black Lives Matter movement and against racism in the wake of the death of George Floyd.
On 27 June 2020, dozens of people staged a demonstration in Wasilla (Alaska) in support of the Back the Blue movement.
On 27 June 2020, an unknown number of people rallied in Cobb (Georgia) [coded as Marietta for GP2] in support of the law enforcement.

On 29 June 2020, people held a protest in Whitefish (Montana) in support of the Black Lives Movement and against police brutality and the death of George Floyd. A white man angrily confronted the protesters and yelled obscenities at them.

On 23 July 2020, over 2000 people demonstrated in Portland - Unspecified (Oregon) in support of the Black Lives Movement. They gathered at the Courthouse for a rally organized by the local NAACP. The demonstration turned violent when a group of rioters began to tear down the fence of the federal building, threw objects and lit fireworks. Women wearing yellow t-shirts, part of 'Wall of Moms', formed a human barricade along the fence's perimeter. The Local police ordered the crowd to leave. Federal officers arrested six people for failing to comply with a lawful order.

source: 11 Alive; Fox30; Atlanta Journal Constitution; WJCL22
notes: On 1 August 2020, a riot broke out at Ware State Prison near Waycross (Georgia). Two prison guards were injured, one hurt in the head and one stabbed and beaten. Three inmates were injured. According to Atlanta Journal Constitution, the prisoners have recently been dissatisfied because the facility was placed on lockdown after an inmate died in, as per officials, a fight with another inmate. Besides, visitations have been cancelled since March due to coronavirus and staffing concerns got worse as guards are either sick with the virus or inmates are in hospitals receiving treatment, requiring guards to accompany them.

source: Salt Lake Tribune; Crowd Counting Consortium; Spectrum; ABC4 Utah
notes: On 2 August 2020, dozens of people took part in 'March for Justice' rally in Cottonwood Heights (Utah) demanding justice for Zane James, a 19-year-old white man shot by local police in 2018. City and state officials, police reform activists, and local business owners were among the demonstrators. According to the police, demonstrators blocked the street and officers reacted by using pepper spray, stun guns, and batons. Demonstrators claimed that officers pushed people, including a city councilwoman, who was also punched in her throat by the local police. According to the Police Department, five officers were injured after being assaulted by demonstrators, resulting in broken ribs, a broken nose, and other injuries. Nine people were arrested.

On 14 August 2020, over 100 people staged a demonstration outside Big Apple Motel in Waterbury (Connecticut) to call for closedown of the motel where, according to the organizer of an online petition 'CRUSH THE APPLE', drugs, sexual assaults and other illegal activity frequently occurred. During the demonstration, demonstrators blocked streets, damaged the electronic billboard sign on the roof of the motel, broke the front windows, damaged property inside the lobby, and one demonstrator threw a metal object to a police officer, and two demonstrators were taken into custody by the police.

On 16 August 2020, about 100 demonstrators gathered in Waterbury (Connecticut) to call for the closure of a local motel. The demonstration turned violent when rioters climbed onto the roof of the motel, damaged its electronic billboard, broke windows, and damaged property inside the building.

On 4 October 2020, a group of white men assaulted two Hispanic men at a bar in Franklin (Tennessee) for speaking Spanish, telling them 'speak fucking English, you're in America'. One of the men suffered a concussion and a broken nose, with an eye socket needing several surgeries to repair. One of the victim is a trumpet player for the Grammy-winning US country band The Mavericks.
